question.problem:
Simplify $tanh\,(\frac{k}{3})$ in terms of $e$ using the definition of the hyperbolic tangent.

$tanh\,(\frac{k}{3})=$

| {{field-1}} |
| --- |
| ${e}^{2k/3}+1$ |
question.worked_solution:
The definition of $\operatorname{tanh}⁡x$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tanh}⁡x & =\frac{{e}^{x}-{e}^{-x}}{{e}^{x}+{e}^{-x}} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2x}-1}{{e}^{2x}+1} \\  & =\frac{1-{e}^{-2x}}{1+{e}^{-2x}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the second definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}tanh\,(\frac{k}{3}) & =\frac{{e}^{2(k/3)}-1}{{e}^{2(k/3)}+1} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2k/3}-1}{{e}^{2k/3}+1}.\end{aligned}
$$
